unit.title: Describing Your World: Ser, Estar, and Haber

lesson.title: Publishing Guía de mi Ciudad: Peer Comments in Spanish
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: This week closes the way real writing actually gets used: read by someone else, who responds to it. Today you turn Wednesday's draft into a finished Guía de mi barrio, then read three classmates' guías and leave real comments in Spanish — not a grade, an actual reaction.

Revise Wednesday's draft with this week's whole toolkit in mind one more time: does it open with identity (ser)? Does it introduce at least two specific features with hay, using un/una rather than el/la? Does it then locate those exact features with estar or estar ubicado, now that they're known? Does it include one sentence about the ambiente or the paisaje? A finished guía should read like an actual short piece someone unfamiliar with your neighborhood could follow and picture.

When you read a classmate's guía, respond in Spanish using sentence starters like these: Me gusta cómo describiste... (I like how you described...) ¿Dónde está exactamente...? (Where exactly is...?) Suena como un barrio... (It sounds like a ... neighborhood.) Yo también tengo/no tengo... cerca de mi casa. (I also have/don't have... near my house.) A genuine comment responds to something specific in the writing — a real question or a real reaction — not a generic 'good job.'

That's the week: from mapping three words on Monday to publishing and reading real responses on Friday. Next week: the people in your life — family, values, and the untranslatable hour Spanish speakers call la sobremesa.

items.prompt: Translate to Spanish: there is, there are

objectives: Revise a neighborhood-description draft into a finished, publishable guía using ser, estar, and hay accurately throughout
Write at least three genuine peer comments in Spanish that respond to specific content in a classmate's guía
materialsNeeded: A way to share writing with at least two other students (printed copies, a shared doc, or reading aloud in a small group)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Complete the vocabulary-recap activity as a warm-up.
2. Revise Wednesday's draft using the explanation block's checklist (identity, hay features, estar locations, ambiente/paisaje).
3. Read the peer-comment-guidance block; practice one comment together on a sample sentence before reading real guías.
4. Share guías with at least two other students (or family members) and exchange comments in Spanish.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview next week's topic: family, values, and la sobremesa.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide the peer-comment sentence starters as a physical reference card during the exchange, rather than expecting them from memory
Ready for more: challenge them to leave one comment that asks a genuine follow-up question requiring more than a yes/no answer
If no peer is available, have the student comment on one of this week's reading passages (Cartagena or Valparaíso) as a stand-in, using the same sentence starters
teacherGuide.answerKey: There is no single correct guía or set of comments — evaluate the revised draft against this week's full ser/estar/hay checklist, and evaluate comments for genuine, specific engagement (a real reaction or question) rather than generic praise.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Closes the week's WA-WL-2015.1.2 arc by moving from interpretive reading (Tuesday) through presentational writing (Wednesday) and speaking (Thursday) to genuine interpersonal exchange in writing, per the scope-and-sequence's Day 5 target ('publish Guía de mi ciudad entries; peer-read three and leave Spanish comments'). The vocabulary recap confirms the week's 7 words are solid before the final application task.

worksheet.title: Publishing Guía de mi Ciudad: Peer Comments in Spanish

generationData.instructions: Use this sheet to revise your guía and plan your peer comments.

rows.problem: List the four checklist items your revised guía needs to include (identity, hay features, estar locations, ambiente/paisaje) and check off each one in your draft.
Write one peer comment you plan to leave using 'Me gusta cómo describiste...'
Write one peer comment using a genuine question: '¿Dónde está...?' or '¿Cómo es...?'
After reading three classmates' guías, which neighborhood sounded most different from yours, and why?
